bug_description.original:
Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5649242005176320

Project: usrsctp
Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer
Fuzz Target: fuzzer_connect
Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_usrsctp
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value
Crash State:
  sctp_find_ifa_by_addr
  sctp_add_remote_addr
  sctp_handle_asconf

Sanitizer: memory
bug_description.normalized: The staged 73-byte witness uses stage byte `0x20`, so `fuzzer_connect` chooses stage 3, injects INIT_ACK and COOKIE_ACK, and then passes the remaining 72 bytes behind a fixed 12-byte common SCTP header into `usrsctp_conninput()`. After that common header the final packet begins with an AUTH chunk `0f 20 00 28` followed by an ASCONF chunk `c1 20 00 20`. In `sctp_process_control()`, the AUTH chunk is handled first; on this userspace fuzz build `sctp_handle_auth()` succeeds and `stcb->asoc.authenticated = 1`, so the later auth-required predicate does not discard the ASCONF chunk. Inside `sctp_handle_asconf()`, the mandatory lookup-address header bytes `20 20 00 0a` are read and `offset` is advanced by the claimed length 10 without validating a real address parameter. At the new offset, bytes `c0 01 00 08 20 20 ff 20` are accepted as an outer `SCTP_ADD_IP_ADDRESS` parameter whose length is only 8. `sctp_m_getptr(m, offset, param_length, aparam_buf)` can return a direct pointer into the contiguous mbuf, so `sctp_process_asconf_add_ip()` immediately reparses the following bytes `00 06 00 14` as a nested `SCTP_IPV6_ADDRESS` parameter of length 20. The vulnerable code has both lengths in hand (`aparam_length == 8`, `param_length == 20`) but never checks that the inner IPv6 parameter fits within the outer ADD_IP parameter. It therefore copies 16 bytes from `v6addr->addr` into `sin6->sin6_addr` even though only the first two of those bytes are inside the packet and the remaining 14 come from the uninitialized tail of the heap mbuf allocated by `m_get()` during `m_copyback()`. `sctp_add_remote_addr()` forwards that sockaddr to `sctp_find_ifa_by_addr()`, where `SCTP6_ARE_ADDR_EQUAL()` reads the poisoned `sin6_addr` and triggers the staged MemorySanitizer `use-of-uninitialized-value`. The staged patch is only a harness mitigation: it adds `usrsctp_sysctl_set_sctp_auth_enable(0);` in `initialize_fuzzer()`, preventing this AUTH-gated ASCONF path from being exercised instead of fixing the parser.

source.description: This is the first project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled final SCTP packet and materializes it into the mbuf chain later parsed as AUTH and ASCONF data.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 73 bytes. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` uses byte 0 only for stage selection (`0x20` -> stage 3), prepends the fixed 12-byte common SCTP header, copies `data[1..72]` behind it, and passes that resulting 84-byte packet as `buffer,length` into `usrsctp_conninput()`.

sink.description: The local-interface lookup compares the copied IPv6 address against registered local addresses. This comparison reads the poisoned `sin6_addr` bytes and is the MemorySanitizer-reported use-of-uninitialized-value sink.

root_cause.code: aparam_length = ntohs(aph->ph.param_length); ph = (struct sctp_paramhdr *)(aph + 1); param_type = ntohs(ph->param_type); param_length = ntohs(ph->param_length);
root_cause.description: The parser reads both the outer ADD_IP length and the nested address-parameter type/length from bytes immediately after the 8-byte outer header, but never verifies that the nested IPv6 parameter fits within the outer parameter before later copying 16 address bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This copy places the attacker-chosen chunk headers and parameter lengths into the mbuf chain `m`; later steps read the AUTH chunk, the lookup-address length `0x000a`, the outer ADD_IP length `0x0008`, and the nested IPv6 length `0x0014` from that packet image.

parser_admitted.description: On the witnessed path the leading AUTH chunk has already set `stcb->asoc.authenticated = 1`, so the auth-required ASCONF predicate at `sctp_input.c:4997-4999` does not skip the following ASCONF chunk and control reaches `sctp_handle_asconf()` here.

coarse_trace.summary: Copies the attacker-controlled final SCTP packet into an mbuf chain whose heap tail remains uninitialized past the copied packet end.
The leading AUTH chunk is accepted and sets `stcb->asoc.authenticated = 1`, which lets the following ASCONF chunk pass the auth-required gate.
ASCONF trusts the lookup-address length 10, then admits a length-8 outer ADD_IP parameter and materializes it as a direct pointer into the contiguous mbuf.
The add-ip parser reparses bytes immediately after that 8-byte outer header as a nested IPv6 parameter of length 20 and copies 16 bytes from beyond packet end into `sin6_addr`.
The local-address comparison reads the poisoned IPv6 address and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled final SCTP packet. The AUTH and ASCONF chunk bytes later parsed on the crashing path are now in mbuf chain `m`.
To extend the chain for the 84-byte packet, `m_copyback()` allocates a fresh heap mbuf. MemorySanitizer traces the later poisoned bytes back to this allocation.

Only the actual packet bytes are copied into the new mbuf. Bytes in the same heap buffer after the copied packet end remain uninitialized, so later reads past packet end still carry the step-2 poison.

The staged packet's leading `0f 20 00 28` AUTH chunk reaches the success arm of the preceding `sctp_handle_auth(...)` call at `sctp_input.c:5631-5632`; on this userspace fuzz build that helper returns success, so this assignment marks the remaining chunks in the packet authenticated.

When the loop reaches the following ASCONF chunk, ASCONF is auth-required. Because step 4 already set `authenticated = 1`, this predicate is false and the ASCONF chunk is not skipped at `goto next_chunk`; control falls through to `case SCTP_ASCONF`.

Inside `sctp_handle_asconf()`, the mandatory lookup-address header bytes `20 20 00 0a` are treated as `p_addr->ph.param_length == 10`. The handler blindly advances `offset` by that claimed length, landing the next parse at bytes `c0 01 00 08 20 20 ff 20`.

At this offset the outer header already parsed from `aph->ph` says type `SCTP_ADD_IP_ADDRESS` and length 8. That 8-byte length passes the generic outer-parameter checks (`offset + param_length <= asconf_limit`, `param_length > sizeof(struct sctp_paramhdr)`), so `sctp_handle_asconf()` requests exactly 8 bytes. Because those bytes are contiguous in the current mbuf, `sctp_m_getptr()` can return a direct pointer into `m` rather than copy into `aparam_buf`, so `aph` aliases `c0 01 00 08 20 20 ff 20` and `aph + 1` points immediately at the following `00 06 00 14` header.

fine_trace.code: aparam_length = ntohs(aph->ph.param_length); ph = (struct sctp_paramhdr *)(aph + 1); param_type = ntohs(ph->param_type); param_length = ntohs(ph->param_length);
fine_trace.note: The callee reparses bytes at `aph + 1` as a nested parameter header: `param_type = SCTP_IPV6_ADDRESS` and `param_length = 20`, while the outer `aparam_length` is still 8. The code never checks that the inner IPv6 parameter fits inside the outer ADD_IP parameter before using it.

In the IPv6 case, `ph` is cast to `v6addr` and 16 bytes are copied from `v6addr->addr` into the temporary sockaddr. Only the first two address bytes are in the staged packet; the remaining 14 come from beyond packet end in the uninitialized mbuf tail, and the saved MSAN trace marks this `memcpy` as the poisoned-value store.
The temporary sockaddr built in step 9 is forwarded into the local-interface lookup path while processing the ADD_IP request.

MemorySanitizer sink. The local-interface comparison reads the copied IPv6 address from step 9, and the uninitialized tail bytes in `addr->sin6_addr` trigger the reported `use-of-uninitialized-value` here.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative runtime evidence is `default_crash_trace.txt` / `sanitizer_trace.txt`, captured while `/out/fuzzer_connect /tmp/poc` processed the staged 73-byte witness. Its first byte is `0x20`, so the harness injects INIT_ACK and COOKIE_ACK before sending bytes 1..72 behind a fixed SCTP common header as the final packet.

format.name: 73-byte stage-3 fuzzer_connect SCTP control packet
format.contract: The verified witness is the staged 73-byte `poc` whose first byte is `0x20`, selecting stage 3. Bytes 1..72 must begin with AUTH `0f 20 00 28` followed by ASCONF `c1 20 00 20`, and the ASCONF payload must contain the exact malformed sequence `20 20 00 0a` (lookup-address length 10), `c0 01 00 08 20 20 ff 20` (outer ADD_IP parameter length 8 plus correlation id), and `00 06 00 14` (nested IPv6 parameter header length 20), so `sctp_process_asconf_add_ip()` copies 16 bytes past the copied packet end into `sin6_addr`.
